chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: 'McGhee Special', writing for Kirk, leaving over money
summary: Kirk lets him play freely and records 'McGhee Special'; he writes arrangements and vocals backing for June Richmond but leaves over pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So I really enjoyed being with Kirk, because he let me play anything I wanted to play. He never said, "Well, I want you to do this, I want you to do that." He said, "Okay, if that's what you want, we'll do it." Which was beautiful. And we came to New York, and they made me play "McGhee Special" ten times before they decided to record it. So I was just on the verge of giving him some, "Fuck it, I don't want to make it, the hell with it," blah-blah-blah, and then the guy said, "Okay, let's make it now."
Oh, I wrote that back there when I was in the band in Detroit.
When you had your own band.

Yeah, that's what I called it, right. But I did that... I just took the book and I put the arrangement in Andy's band, and Andy featured me on it. You know, after hearing it, he liked it, and he said, "Well, it looks good; we'll keep it in the book." And most of my music he liked, you know. I wrote "Seven Come Eleven" and things that Benny made...

Yeah, I wrote that up for him. And quite a few things I wrote. And all of June Richmond's vocals I was doing. With Andy I was having a ball, man. The money was nice, and every time I asked for a raise I'd get one. So I got it up to thirty-five dollars a night...
And the band was a pretty happy band, I guess, with each other...
With each other. We were getting along beautiful. In fact, I hated to leave the band, but I really left the band on account of money.
